comparison: Strong disagreement on T cell classification (C42-C44). OpenEval finds claims supported based on canonical markers and appropriate annotations. Peer reviewers identify multiple critical issues: all CD4+ T cells incorrectly classified as Tregs, missing T-helper cells, and cytotoxic T cells expressing exhaustion markers, indicating problematic cell type definitions.

Disagreement on neutrophil classification (C45-C50). OpenEval finds claims supported based on consensus markers and prognostic associations. Peer reviewers raise concerns about clustering artifacts (obviously different clusters grouped together, potential doublets with cancer cells), questioning the underlying cell type definitions despite acknowledging prognostic associations.

Agreement on plasma/B cell analysis (C51-C53). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support these findings. OpenEval notes the functional role remains unclear, while peer reviewers do not raise specific concerns about this cluster's identification or characterization.

Partial agreement on basic cellular composition (C20-C25 overlap, C26-C28 in R1 only). Both acknowledge the dataset quality and basic composition findings. OpenEval finds all claims supported. Peer reviewers support the data value but raise methodological concerns about batch correction and clustering parameters that don't dispute the core findings.

Agreement on comparative cell composition data (C26-C28). OpenEval finds the statistical differences between ADC and SCC supported by Figure 1F. Peer reviewers include these claims in their overall acceptance of the cellular composition findings, with no specific challenges to these comparative results.

Strong disagreement on Epi_10_CYSTM1 cluster (C29-C31). OpenEval finds claims supported by figures and exclusive presence in ADC. Peer reviewers express serious concerns: cluster is essentially exclusive to one sample, questions about whether it represents epithelial or dendritic/macrophage cells, and concerns about generalizability despite acknowledging IF validation.

Disagreement on malignancy scoring and functional predictions (C32-C34). OpenEval finds claims supported by computational analysis but notes experimental validation would strengthen them. Peer reviewers' concerns about the underlying Epi_10_CYSTM1 cluster (same result R2) cast doubt on these functional interpretations.

Disagreement on SLC26A3 as biomarker (C35-C37, with C35 overlap). OpenEval finds IHC validation and statistical associations support the claims, noting appropriate cautious language. Peer reviewers question the mechanistic link to Epi_10_CYSTM1, noting most cluster markers were not predictive and questioning why SLC26A3 is rare in scRNA-seq but abundant in IHC.

Disagreement on SLC26A3 biomarker claims (C36-C37 overlap, C35 in R10 only). OpenEval supports based on IHC validation and statistical significance. Peer reviewers acknowledge clinical correlations but express significant concerns about the linkage between Epi_10_CYSTM1 cluster and SLC26A3, questioning specificity and mechanistic connection.

Partial agreement on HPV status and clinical findings (C38-C41). OpenEval finds claims supported by two independent cohorts with appropriate statistical analysis. Peer reviewers' concerns focus more on the biomarker linkage (C36-C37) rather than the HPV-related clinical observations, suggesting implicit acceptance of these epidemiological findings.

Disagreement on cell-cell interaction claims (C54-C56, C58 overlap). OpenEval finds claims supported by CellChat analysis and IF validation, noting TGFβ pathway is inferred. Peer reviewers criticize causal language, emphasizing these are correlative findings showing co-localization but insufficient for mechanistic claims without functional experiments.

Disagreement on specific interaction associations (C57, C59). OpenEval finds spatial co-localization data supportive. Peer reviewers acknowledge IF data but question mechanistic interpretation in context of broader concerns about Epi_10_CYSTM1 cluster and over-interpretation without functional validation.

Agreement on uncertainty of mechanistic claims (C70-C71, C74-C76 overlap). Both identify these as interpretive hypotheses. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable interpretations but speculative causal relationships requiring functional validation. Peer reviewers similarly emphasize correlative nature and criticize causal language without functional experiments.

Agreement on uncertainty of neutrophil mechanistic claims (C72-C73). Both find these claims inferential. OpenEval rates broader mechanistic hypotheses as UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewers note these are based on correlative data with concerns about neutrophil clustering artifacts and over-interpretation without functional validation.

OpenEval finds background/context claims (C1-C3, C60-C62) supported by appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on data interpretation rather than background literature support.

OpenEval finds general knowledge claims about ADC characteristics (C4-C9) supported, with C9 cited to Sasieni et al. 2009. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these background claims were not challenged by reviewers.

OpenEval finds clinical problem motivation claims (C10-C13) supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers did not dispute the background rationale for biomarker research.

OpenEval finds HPV status importance claims (C14-C16) supported by recent literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these background claims establishing analytical framework were not challenged.

OpenEval finds tumor immune microenvironment rationale claims (C17-C19) supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on data analysis rather than background justification.

OpenEval finds mechanistic background claims (C63-C69) supported by published literature providing context for result interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these literature-based contextual claims were not disputed.
